title: SEC1: g_tls_safe_mode never reset on cleanup
description: g_tls_safe_mode (crypto2dev_port.c) is set to 1 by wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid() and wc_crypto2dev_assign_devid_ssl() but is never cleared by wc_crypto2dev_cleanup(). This means: (1) After a cleanup+reinit cycle (e.g., in tests or long-lived daemons that restart the subsystem), TLS-safe mode remains permanently engaged even if the new use is non-TLS. (2) There is no way to use crypto2dev for hardware hash offload in a process that has ever called the TLS integration helper, making the two modes mutually exclusive with no recovery path. (3) If the callback is registered directly via wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice (bypassing the helpers), the flag stays 0 and TLS transcript hashes will incorrectly route to hardware, causing silent corruption. The global flag is also process-wide: a multi-tenant library use where one context wants TLS-safe mode and another does not is impossible. A per-registration context flag (passed via the ctx pointer to wc_CryptoCb_RegisterDevice) would solve this without global state.
